exposure: early short course (7 days) of intranasal oxytocin (OT) treatment
outcome: total communication score (Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales-2nd edition)
socialization score (Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales-2nd edition)
endocrine profile (circulating IGF-1, acylated ghrelin levels)
cohort: The study included 34 children aged 3-4 years with Prader-Willi syndrome, 17 of whom had received early intranasal oxytocin treatment as infants and 17 who were non-exposed controls.
finding: Early intranasal oxytocin treatment in infants with Prader-Willi syndrome was found to be safe up to 3-4 years of age and associated with better social, endocrine, and metabolic outcomes, including higher IGF-1 and HDL cholesterol, lower acylated ghrelin levels, and higher connectivity of the orbitofrontal cortex.
